name: What causes a sewer smell in the bathroom?

mainEntity.name: What causes a sewer smell in the bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: A sewer smell in your bathroom usually indicates a problem with the plumbing system. Common causes include a dry P-trap (the U-shaped pipe under sinks and drains), which allows sewer gases to escape. Other issues can be a cracked or improperly sealed wax ring around the toilet, a clogged or blocked vent pipe that prevents proper air circulation, or a damaged sewer line. Sometimes, a poorly installed or rarely used drain can also contribute to the odor. Identifying the exact source is crucial for effective remediation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sewer smells are often caused by a dry P-trap, a faulty toilet wax ring, a clogged vent pipe, or a damaged sewer line. These issues allow sewer gases into your home.
